description_target.ambiguity_notes: The black and gray field is dense noise rather than a zero background around isolated fragments. Multiple valid 3x3 candidates can share red cells. The executable rule therefore ranks all candidates by red count and reading order, then greedily rejects later candidates that reuse any already covered red cell; recoloring every locally valid window independently is incorrect.
negative_constraints: Do not require a candidate window to be isolated from surrounding black or gray noise.
Do not select a window whose center is red or whose 3x3 cells contain any value other than 2 or 5.
Do not process overlapping candidates independently; reject a lower-priority candidate when any of its red cells was already covered.
Do not recolor red cells or cells outside selected windows.
Do not use numeric color order to break ties; equal red counts use top-left reading order.
solution_steps: Enumerate every 3x3 window whose nine cells are all red 2 or gray 5, whose center is gray 5, and which contains at least one red cell.
Sort candidates by decreasing number of red cells, breaking equal-count ties by the top-left coordinate in reading order.
Walk that order greedily. Keep a candidate only if none of its red cells belongs to an earlier kept candidate; otherwise skip it.
For each kept candidate, preserve every red cell, recolor its gray center yellow 4, and recolor its other gray cells orange 7.
Leave the dense black/gray noise outside selected windows unchanged.
description_target.target_text: Scan the dense 19x19 black, red, and gray scene for every 3x3 window made only of red 2 and gray 5 that has a gray center and at least one red cell. Rank these candidates by descending red-cell count, then by top-left reading order. Greedily keep a candidate only when none of its red cells was covered by an earlier winner. In every kept window, preserve red cells, turn the gray center yellow 4, turn the other gray cells orange 7, and leave all outside noise unchanged.
